convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'Arrows_Curves' indicator (unknown custom indicator with 4 proprietary buffers) and #include <TradeAlgorithms.mqh> external library for order management. Both require manual Python reimplementation of the indicator logic and trade helper functions.

other_exits: Stop channel exit: historical scan of SellStop buffer (index 2) or Buy signal re-occurrence triggers short close; BuyStop buffer (index 3) or Sell signal re-occurrence triggers long close. Scans bars from SignalBar forward until condition found.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM<0 means fixed lot size equal to abs(MM); MM>0 means deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: The Arrows_Curves custom indicator has 4 buffers: buffer0=Sell signal, buffer1=Buy signal, buffer2=SellStop (exit for shorts), buffer3=BuyStop (exit for longs). The exit logic scans forward through historical bars from SignalBar to find the first non-zero/non-EMPTY_VALUE stop signal OR a reverse signal to generate close signals when no direct close signal is present. This historical scan (loop from SignalBar to Bars_) is non-standard and must be carefully replicated. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh include provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar, and GlobalVariableDel_ helper functions. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar. The relay parameter shifts the indicator's lookback in history.
python_conversion_notes: Two major hurdles: (1) The Arrows_Curves custom indicator algorithm must be obtained/reverse-engineered to compute the 4 signal buffers in Python. Without the indicator source, the buy/sell/stop signals cannot be reproduced. (2) The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library functions for order management need Python equivalents, but these are standard wrappers around CTrade. The signal logic itself is straightforward: buy when buffer1 is non-empty, sell when buffer0 is non-empty, close via signal reversal or stop buffer detection. The historical bar scan for stop signals is the trickiest part and must preserve exact iteration semantics. The MM parameter dual-behavior (negative=lot, positive=deposit fraction) must be handled in position sizing code.
